text:
What use, rosebush, is boasting of beauty, if scarcely born you begin to die? Your blush, alive and dead, makes us weep and laugh in one day or one sun: from East to sunset your beauty passes in one step, your perfection in less. Rosebush, boast less among the pinks, for tomorrow those now roses will be thorns.

Your rank gives no great advantage: if dawn is your mantle, night is your shroud. No flower is so lowly it will not outlive you, and the mallow, hair of a clod, laughs at your pretensions as dawn's descendant. Rosebush, boast less among the pinks, for tomorrow those now roses will be thorns.

translation.title: Lyrical Refrain
